analysis.first_pass: The joint roots strengthen the source hypotheses: both require a globally complete manifold, and the root containing a limit also assumes nonnegative Ricci curvature. Its limit follows directly from hprod.small_radius_normalization after rewriting hCnorm, so this part of the source conclusion is supplied as an input. The stated limit uses the flat model k = 0; the other root supplies monotonicity but no limit. Thus the pair does not establish the full Bishop-Gromov theorem under its stated local Ricci lower-bound hypotheses.
analysis.second_pass: The review considers the two roots jointly and grants the intended geometric interpretation of their volume and curvature constructions for the decisive comparison. The first root does not assume nonnegative Ricci, but it has no limit conclusion. The second root requires hric0 for its whole conjunction, including the limit, rather than only for the nonnegative-Ricci corollary. Its limit is precisely the producer field after the hCnorm rewrite. The flat-model limit can in principle be transferred to general k using model-volume asymptotics; the verdict does not treat the denominator difference alone as an irreparable mismatch. Likewise, measurability, the Levi-Civita property, connectedness reductions, dimension conventions, and closed-ball versus open-ball bounds are not used as independent decisive defects. The global completeness restriction and the producer-dependent, nonnegative-Ricci-only limit coverage already fail the full source scope. These may be useful conditional lemmas; the whole theorem is not claimed to be tautological or false.

The open-disk and hyperbolic examples are mathematical applicability checks, not compiled Lean countermodels. No fresh Lean proof, volume-normalization equivalence, or full upstream proof was certified. Proof-erasure sorries are not misalignment evidence. applicability_witnesses.name: Incomplete flat open disk with a relatively compact ball
applicability_witnesses.setup: M = {x in R^2 : ||x|| < 1}, with its ordinary Euclidean Riemannian metric; p = 0, R = 1/2, k = 0.
applicability_witnesses.source_hypotheses: The closure in M of B(p,1/2) is the closed Euclidean disk of radius 1/2, compact and contained in M. Ricci curvature vanishes. The intrinsic distance is Euclidean because the disk is convex.
applicability_witnesses.formal_exclusion: M is not complete: (1 - 1/m, 0), m >= 2, is Cauchy with its Euclidean limit outside M. Both selected roots require CompleteSpace M.
applicability_witnesses.scope: Exhibits a valid source instance excluded by both selected signatures; not a counterexample to the conditional Lean conclusions.

applicability_witnesses.name: Negative-curvature case excluded from the packaged limit
applicability_witnesses.setup: The complete hyperbolic plane of sectional curvature -1; k = 1 and any finite positive R.
applicability_witnesses.source_hypotheses: In dimension 2, Ric(v,v) = -g(v,v), so the source lower bound holds with equality. Metric balls have compact closure.
applicability_witnesses.formal_exclusion: For any nonzero v, hric0 would require 0 <= -g(v,v), which fails. The first root can supply only monotonicity; the root containing the limit cannot be applied under these source hypotheses.
applicability_witnesses.scope: A mathematical check that hric0 is stronger than the source lower bound; no full Lean instantiation is claimed.

alternative_interpretations: As conditional lemmas for a globally complete manifold with supplied analytic producers, the declarations can be useful. The bound informal record explicitly covers the full local theorem, not only that conditional scope.

Flat and curved model denominators have the same small-radius leading term; a transfer lemma could address that denominator difference. It would not remove the existing producer premise or make global completeness follow from the local source assumptions.
The code now binds the ambient distance to g through IsRiemannianDist. The arbitrary-density objection from FM-BISHOP-before must not simply be copied to this case.

This review does not assert a fully normalized canonical-volume identification for the gpHaar-based construction. The decisive hypothesis and output discrepancies do not depend on resolving that additional issue.
